title: TACACS+ (AAA server group)
description: Cisco IOS XR devices can use the TACACS+ protocol to communicate with a central AAA server. Using a central authentication store ensures that all administrative actions are tied to named users, making the tracking of changes much easier. It also makes tracking compromised accounts and malicious activities much easier. Central authentication is key as it minimizes the effort in managing named user accounts. Keeping local admin accounts opens the door to all the issues inherent in shared accounts, namely: - Errors in implementation being done by generic admin accounts, which ... Passes with two or more 'tacacs-server host' entries referenced by an 'aaa group server tacacs+', or when RADIUS (and no TACACS+) is used instead. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.1.1.1 TACACS+

Using a central authentication store ensures that all administrative actions are tied to named users, making the tracking of changes much easier. Keeping local admin accounts opens the door to all the issues inherent in shared accounts, namely: - Errors in implementation being done by generic admin accounts, which ... Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.1.1.2 RADIUS

remediation.command: For complete instructions how to configure AAA please refer to the configuration guide. Below you can find some minimum config snippets to implement a radius or tacacs+ server group. radius-server host {radius_ip_address} key {radius_key} aaa group server radius {radius_group_name} server radius_ip_address}

title: console authentication
description: Authenticate management access to the network devices. Typically a central authentication store combined with a fallback mechanism should be implemented to allow emergency access, in case the central authentication servers are not available. Management access to network devices must be authenticated. The default under AAA (local or network) is to require users to log in using a valid user name and password. This rule applies for both local and network AAA. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.1.2.1 console authentication

remediation.command:
! Configure an authentication list that references the AAA group that was created in the prerequisites. AAA lists are prioritized list of databases. If the system is unable to use a database, it automatically rolls over to the next database on the list. If the authentication, authorization, or accounting request is rejected by any database, the rollover does not occur and the request is rejected. It is common to include "local" as the last entry in the list, to allow access to manage the device even if all servers from the AAA group are unavailable. Note that it also means that if an attacker can DoS the AAA Servers, they can start to try authenticate locally as well. Hence, always ensure to use strong passwords for local users.
aaa authentication login default group {tacacs_group|radius_group} local Above configuration authenticates first against a central aaa group and uses local user accounts as fallback. Ensure the above list is referenced under the line templates:
line console login authentication default Ensure the vty pool references the above line template:
vty-pool default 0 4 line-template default

This rule applies for both local and network AAA. Fails if no line template exists or any 'line default'/'line template' lacks 'login authentication <list>'. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.1.2.2 vty line authentication

Note that it also means that if an attacker can DoS the AAA Servers, they can start to try authenticate locally as well. Hence, always ensure to use strong passwords for local users.
aaa authentication login default group {tacacs_group|radius_group} local Above configuration authenticates first against a central aaa group and uses local user accounts as fallback. Ensure the above list is referenced under the line templates:

title: Set 'seconds' for 'ssh timeout' for 60 seconds or less
description: The time interval that the router waits for the SSH client to respond before disconnecting an uncompleted login attempt. This reduces the risk of an administrator leaving an authenticated session logged in for an extended period of time. CIS Recommends 60 seconds or less. The default is not shown; fails only if 'ssh timeout' is above 60 seconds. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.2.3 Set 'seconds' for 'ssh timeout' for 60 seconds or less

remediation.command:
! Configure the SSH timeout
ssh timeout {ssh_timeout}

title: Unset 'private' for 'snmp-server community'
description: An SNMP community string permits read-only access to all objects. The default community string "private" is well known. Using easy to guess, well known community string poses a threat that an attacker can effortlessly gain unauthorized access to the device. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.5.1 Unset 'private' for 'snmp-server community'

remediation.command:
! Disable the default SNMP community string private
no snmp-server community {community_string}

title: Do not set 'RW' for any 'snmp-server community'
description: Specifies read-write access. Authorized management stations can both retrieve and modify MIB objects. Enabling SNMP read-write enables remote management of the device. Unless absolutely necessary, do not allow simple network management protocol (SNMP) write access. CIS marks this Manual; automated as a config-line check. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.5.3 Do not set 'RW' for any 'snmp-server community'

remediation.command:
! Disable SNMP write access.
no snmp-server community {community_string}

title: Set the ACL for each 'snmp-server community'
description: This feature specifies a list of IP addresses that are allowed to use the community string to gain access to the SNMP agent. If ACLs are not applied, then anyone with a valid SNMP community string can potentially monitor and manage the router. An ACL should be defined and applied for all SNMP access to limit access to a small number of authorized management stations segmented in a ... CIS marks this Manual; automated: fails if a community line carries no IPv4/IPv6 ACL. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.5.4 Set the ACL for each 'snmp-server community'

remediation.command:
! Configure authorized SNMP community string and restrict access to authorized management systems.
snmp-server community {community_string} RO IPv4 {snmp_access-list}

title: Disable Telnet Access
description: Telnet is a clear-text administrative protocol. As such, both the credentials used to establish the session and all commands and data within the session are readable in clear-text, so can be intercepted or modified by an attacker. Telnet doesn't natively support encryption or message integrity checks. Hence, any transmitted information (including credentials) is exposed to an attacker that gains access to the communication. Fails if a telnet server is enabled or a line template allows anything other than 'transport input ssh'. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.6.1 Disable Telnet Access

remediation.command: It's recommended to restrict VTYs to SSH for management access and not allow this device to SSH to other devices: vty-pool default 0 4 line-template default line default transport input ssh transport output none

title: Restrict VTY Access
description: VTY access can be restricted via access-lists to limit from which the source addresses a management session to the device can be established. VTY ACLs control what addresses may attempt to log in to the router. Configuring VTY lines to use an ACL, restricts the sources where a user can manage the device. CIS marks this Manual; automated: requires an 'access-class ingress <acl>' on a line template. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.6.2 Restrict VTY Access

remediation.command: Define ACLs which match the allowed sources. To restrict access of incoming or outgoing connections over IPv4 and IPv6, the IPv4 access list and IPv6 access list must share the same name: ipv4 access-list ACL-VTY-IN 10 permit ipv4 192.168.1.0/24 any 1000 deny ipv4 any any log icmp-off ipv6 access-list ACL-VTY-IN 10 permit ipv6 2001:db8::/64 any 1000 deny any any log icmp-off Apply the ACL on the line template: vty-pool default 0 4 line-template default line default access-class ingress ACL-VTY-IN Alternatively you can implement restrictions on the SSH Server which allows both IPv4 and IPv6. Note that SSH could be also used for Netconf, so the ACL might need to include additional sources which do not apply for VTY access only. ssh server ipv4 access-list ACL-VTY-IN ipv6 access-list ACL-VTY-IN

title: Enable AES Password Encryption
description: You can enable strong, reversible 128-bit Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) password encryption, also known as type-6 encryption. To start using type-6 encryption, you must enable the AES password encryption feature and configure a master encryption key, which is used to encrypt and decrypt passwords. Encryption of passwords is used to protect it from being sent over the wire cleartext or being accidentally exposed when sharing device configurations with third parties. CIS assessment: Manual. Reported as SKIP with review instructions.
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.8.1 Enable AES Password Encryption

audit.command: CIS assessment: Manual. Just verifying the running configuration might not be sufficient because it could be that no masterkey has been set. IOSXR# show run formal | i password6 password6 encryption aes Use the following show command to see if encryption is enabled and functional. Only when all three status are "Enabled" the feature is fully working.

remediation.command:
! Define a password encryption key
key config-key password-encryption New password Requirements: Min-length 6, Max-length 64 Characters restricted to [A-Z][a-z][0-9] Enter new key : Enter confirm key : Master key operation is started in background Enable aes config password encryption /* Enable Type 6 password encryption */
configure
password6 encryption aes
commit

title: Set username secret for all local users
description: A root-system user with a normal password will not be authenticated because the normal password is two-way encrypted and poses a security risk because the password information is stored in the flash disk, which can be easily decrypted. Secrets are one-way encrypted and cannot be easily reverted without brute-forcing. Secrets use a one-way cryptographic hash. CIS marks this Manual; automated: fails if any local username has no 'secret'. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.8.2 Set username secret for all local users

title: Configure a Password Policy
description: Because passwords are stored only in revertible type 7 format, please consider not applying this recommendation and using secrets instead. This only applies if you absolutely need to configure "password" instead of "secret" for local users. Cisco IOS XR Software introduces advanced AAA password strengthening policy and security mechanism to store, retrieve and provide rules or policy to specify user passwords. Strong passwords are important because they help prevent unauthorized access to devices and the network. Even if a central authentication source is used, if that service is not available the fall-back authentication is often to local credentials. CIS assessment: Manual. Reported as SKIP with review instructions.
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.8.3 Configure a Password Policy

audit.command: CIS assessment: Manual. IOSXR#sh run aaa aaa password-policy {password_policy} lifetime months 3 max-length 25 min-length 18 lockout-time days 1 min-char-change 5 authen-max-attempts 3 ! username {local_username} group root-lr group cisco-support secret {local_password} The policy is only in effect when it is also applied under a "username" section.

remediation.command:
! Use the following configuration to enable a password policy. Choose values according to established guidelines of your organization.
configure
aaa password-policy {password_policy}
min-length 8
max-length 25
lifetime months 3
min-char-change 5
authen-max-attempts 3
lockout-time days 1
username {local_username} password-policy {password_policy} password 0 {local_password}
commit

title: Configure Authorization
description: Command authorization allows restricting specific users to specific command sets that they can use on the device. Command authorization is a complex endeavor and is very rarely implemented. Usually, the TACACS+ protocol is used with a central AAA server. Command authorization allows the implementation of fine-grained role-based access control concepts. Fails if no 'aaa authorization commands' list exists or a console/line template does not reference one. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.1.3.1 Configure Authorization

remediation.command: Currently CIS makes no recommendations how to implement command authorization. Roles and access-privileges should be defined in collaboration with your operations and security teams.

Each accounting record contains accounting AV pairs and is stored on the security server. Authentication, authorization and accounting (AAA) systems provide an authoritative source for managing and monitoring access for devices. Centralizing control improves consistency of access control, the services that may be accessed once authenticated and ... title: Local users, groups and tasks
description: To provide controlled access to the XR and System Admin configurations on the router, user profiles are created with assigned privileges. The privileges are specified using command rules and data rules. The authentication, authorization, and accounting (aaa) commands are used for the creation of users, groups, command rules, and data rules. The aaa commands are also used for changing the disaster-recovery password. IOS-XR has a very strong embedded mechanism to do user authentication and authorization. While XR does not have the concept of privilege-levels as what IOS had, the embedded user task group management is extremely strong allow for the creation of different ... CIS assessment: Manual. Reported as SKIP with review instructions.
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.1.5 Local users, groups and tasks

title: Set 'modulus' to greater than or equal to 2048 for 'crypto key generate rsa'
description: Use this command to generate RSA key pairs for your Cisco device. RSA keys are generated in pairs--one public RSA key and one private RSA key. An RSA key pair is a prerequisite for setting up SSH and should be at least 2048 bits. NOTE: IOS does NOT display the modulus bit value in the Audit Procedure. CIS assessment: Manual. Reported as SKIP with review instructions.
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.2.2 Set 'modulus' to greater than or equal to 2048 for 'crypto key generate rsa'

audit.command: CIS assessment: Manual. Perform the following to determine if the RSA key pair is configured: IOSXR#sh crypto key mypubkey rsa Wed Jul 19 18:09:46.009 UTC Key label: the_default Type : RSA General purpose Size : 2048 Created : 16:25:09 UTC Wed Jul 19 2023

remediation.command:
! Generate an RSA key pair for the router.
crypto key generate rsa general-keys Wed Jul 19 18:10:51.633 UTC The name for the keys will be: the_default % You already have keys defined for the_default Do you really want to replace them? [yes/no]: yes Choose the size of the key modulus in the range of 512 to 4096 for your General Purpose Keypair. Choosing a key modulus greater than 512 may take a few minutes. How many bits in the modulus [2048]: Generating RSA keys ... Done w/ crypto generate keypair [OK]

It is useful only in network monitoring and troubleshooting situations but is considered a security risk because of the amount of ... title: Disable TCP and UDP small servers
description: TCP and UDP small servers are servers (daemons, in Unix parlance) that run in the router which are useful for diagnostics. TCP Small Servers The TCP small servers are: Echo: Echoes back whatever you type through the telnet x.x.x.x echo command. Chargen: Generates a stream of ASCII data. Use the telnet x.x.x.x chargen command. Discard: Throws away whatever you type. CIS marks this Manual; automated as a config-line check. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.3.2 Disable TCP and UDP small servers

remediation.command:

no service ipv4 udp-small-servers max-servers 10
commit

This configuration determines the severity of messages that will generate console messages. Logging to console should be limited only to those messages required for immediate troubleshooting while logged into the device. CIS marks this Manual; automated as a config-line check. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.4.3 Set 'logging console critical'

title: Set IP address for 'logging host'
description: Log system messages and debug output to a remote host. Cisco routers can send their log messages to a Unix-style Syslog service. A syslog service simply accepts messages and stores them in files or prints them according to a simple configuration file. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.4.4 Set IP address for 'logging host'

remediation.command:
! Designate one or more syslog servers by IP address.
logging host {syslog_server}

title: Set 'logging trap informational'
description: Limit messages logged to the syslog servers based on severity level informational. This determines the severity of messages that will generate simple network management protocol (SNMP) trap and or syslog messages. This setting should be set to either "debugging" (7) or "informational" (6), but no lower. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.4.5 Set 'logging trap informational'

remediation.command:
! Configure SNMP trap and syslog logging level.
logging trap informational

title: Set 'logging source interface'
description: Specify the source IPv4 or IPv6 address of system logging packets. This is required so that the router sends log messages to the logging server from a consistent IP address. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.4.7 Set 'logging source interface'

remediation.command:
! Bind logging to the loopback interface.
logging source-interface {logging_source_interface}

title: Set 'snmp-server host' when using SNMP
description: SNMP notifications can be sent as traps to authorized management systems. If SNMP is enabled for device management and device alerts are required, then ensure the device is configured to submit traps only to authorize management systems. CIS marks this Manual; automated: fails when SNMP is configured but no 'snmp-server host' exists. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.5.5 Set 'snmp-server host' when using SNMP

remediation.command:
! Configure authorized SNMP trap community string and restrict sending messages to authorized management systems.
snmp-server host {ip_address} version {snmp_version} {encryption-type} {trap_community_string}

title: Set 'snmp-server enable traps snmp'
description: SNMP notifications can be sent as traps to authorized management systems. SNMP has the ability to submit traps . Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.5.6 Set 'snmp-server enable traps snmp'

remediation.command:
! Enable SNMP traps.
snmp-server traps snmp authentication

title: Set 'priv' for each 'snmp-server group' using SNMPv3
description: Specifies authentication of a packet with encryption when using SNMPv3. SNMPv3 provides much improved security over previous versions by offering options for Authentication and Encryption of messages. When configuring a user for SNMPv3 you have the option of using a range of encryption schemes, or no encryption at all, to protect ... remediation.command:

title: Require 'aes 128' as minimum for 'snmp-server user' when using SNMPv3
description: Specify the use of a minimum of 128-bit AES algorithm for encryption when using SNMPv3. SNMPv3 provides much improved security over previous versions by offering options for Authentication and Encryption of messages. When configuring a user for SNMPv3 you have the option of using a range of encryption schemes, or no encryption at all, to protect ... Fails if any SNMPv3 user is configured without 'priv aes <bits>'. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.5.8 Require 'aes 128' as minimum for 'snmp-server user' when using SNMPv3

remediation.command:
! For each SNMPv3 user created on your router add privacy options by issuing the following command.
snmp-server user {snmp_user_name} {snmp_group_name} v3 auth sha {snmp_auth_password} priv aes 128 {snmp_priv_password} ipv4 {snmp_access-list}

title: Ensure Exec Timeout for Console Sessions is set
description: Verify device is configured to automatically disconnect console sessions after a defined maximum session time, set in minutes. Note there are 3 different timeout values: - absolute-timeout: terminate the connection after the specified time has elapsed, regardless of whether the connection is being used at the time of termination. This prevents unauthorized users from misusing abandoned sessions. For example, if the network administrator disconnects leaving a console session open, that session will remain open (in the same state and privilege level) for the next person who connects a ... Default 10 minutes applies when unset; fails if the console timeout is above 10 minutes or disabled. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.6.3 Ensure Exec Timeout for Console Sessions is set

remediation.command: vty-pool default 0 4 line-template default line default exec-timeout 10 0

title: Management plane protection
description: The Management Plane Protection (MPP) feature provides the capability to restrict the interfaces on which network management packets are allowed to enter a device. The MPP feature allows a network operator to designate one or more router interfaces as management interfaces. The MPP protection feature, as well as all the management protocols under MPP, are disabled by default. This is part of the MPP setup. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.9 Management plane protection

remediation.command:
! Configure the management plane so that only certain protocols connectced to certain interfaces can access this IOS-XR device.
control-plane
management-plane
inband
interface {interface} allow {protocol} peer address ipv4 {IP_address}
out-of-band
interface {interface} allow {protocol} peer address ipv4 {IP_address}

title: Key chains (routing protocols)
description: Keychain management is a common method of authentication to configure shared secrets on all entities that exchange secrets such as keys, before establishing trust with each other. Routing protocols and network management applications on Cisco IOS XR software often use authentication to enhance security while communicating with peers. The keychain by itself has no relevance; therefore, it must be used by an application that needs to communicate by using the keys (for authentication) with its peers. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.1.6 Key chains

title: Set 'ntp authenticate'
description: Enable NTP authentication. Using authenticated NTP ensures the Cisco device only permits time updates from authorized NTP servers. CIS marks this Manual; automated as a config check under 'ntp'. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.2.1.1 Set 'ntp authenticate'

remediation.command:
! Configure NTP authentication:
ntp authenticate

title: Set the 'ntp trusted-key'
description: Ensure you authenticate the identity of a system to which Network Time Protocol (NTP) will synchronize. This authentication function provides protection against accidentally synchronizing the system to another system that is not trusted, because the other system must know the correct authentication key. CIS marks this Manual; automated as a config check under 'ntp'. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.2.1.3 Set the 'ntp trusted-key'

remediation.command:
! Configure the NTP trusted key using the following command
ntp trusted-key {ntp_key_id}

title: Set 'key' for each 'ntp server'
description: Specifies the authentication key for NTP. This authentication feature provides protection against accidentally synchronizing the ntp system to another system that is not trusted, because the other system must know the correct authentication key. CIS marks this Manual; automated: fails if any NTP server has no 'key <id>'. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.2.1.4 Set 'key' for each 'ntp server'

remediation.command:
! Configure each NTP Server to use a key ring using the following command.
ntp server {ntp-server_ip_address} key {ntp_key_id}

title: Set 'ip address' for 'ntp server'
description: Use this command if you want to allow the system to synchronize the system software clock with the specified NTP server. To ensure that the time on your Cisco router is consistent with other devices in your network, at least two (and preferably at least three) NTP Server/s external to the router should be configured. CIS marks this Manual; automated as a config check under 'ntp'. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.2.2 Set 'ip address' for 'ntp server'

remediation.command:
! Configure theexternal NTP Server using the following commands
ntp server {ntp-server_ip_address} key {ntp_key_id}

description: Configure the system to apply a time stamp to debugging messages or system logging messages. Including timestamps in log messages allows correlating events and tracing network attacks across multiple devices. Enabling service timestamp to mark the time log messages were generated simplifies obtaining a holistic view of events enabling faster ... Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').

title: Pre-authentication Banner
description: A pre-authentication banner is displayed when a terminal connects, before a login occurs. This banner is useful for sending messages that affect all users (such as impending system shutdowns). This banner can also be used to notify unauthorized users of any penalties to accessing the device, or any logging that may be configured. Network banners are electronic messages that provide notice of legal rights to users of computer networks. From a legal standpoint, banners have following primary functions. Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.7.1 Pre-authentication Banner

remediation.command:
! Configure a login banner as shown below. The delimiter character shown is a "^", but any character can serve as a delimiter.
banner login ^ {login_banner} ^

title: Post-authentication Banner
description: A post-authentication banner is displayed to the user after a successful login. It can also serve as a legal notice to authorized users of the equipment to notify them of any logging that may be configured. This banner is not appropriate to notify unauthorized users of any penalties to accessing the device, because after successful login corresponding laws might have already been violated. Post-authentication banners can be used to reduce the risk of human error. For example by highlighting the current environment (Production or Lab). Audited against the hierarchical output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; not 'show running-config formal').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XR 7.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.7.2 Post-authentication Banner

remediation.command:
! Configure an exec banner as shown below. The delimiter character shown is a "^", but any character can serve as a delimiter.
banner exec ^ {exec_banner} ^
